description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts. Network service discovery can involve probing ports, services, or hosts to identify available network services.
network_observable_behavior: Rapid probing within a short time window
netvision_relevance: Highly relevant because NetVision represents traffic within 5-minute temporal windows and includes connection, destination-port, protocol, packet, and flow-level statistics.
evidence_limitation: Flow-level traffic can indicate scanning or discovery-like behavior, but it cannot independently prove malicious intent or identify the exact scanning tool.

description: Adversaries may perform Network Denial of Service to degrade or block the availability of a targeted system or network resource through excessive network activity.
network_observable_behavior: Concentrated traffic over a short temporal interval
netvision_relevance: Highly relevant because NetVision contains packet-count, byte-volume, packet-rate, flow-count, and temporal aggregation features.
evidence_limitation: High traffic volume may also occur during legitimate traffic bursts. Network volume alone cannot prove that a denial-of-service attack is occurring.

description: Adversaries may directly send a high volume of network traffic toward a target in an attempt to degrade or disrupt its availability.
netvision_relevance: Relevant because NetVision contains temporal traffic volume, packet-rate, flow-count, and duration features that can provide evidence of concentrated network floods.
evidence_limitation: Flow features alone may not establish that traffic was deliberately generated as a flood or determine whether the activity originated from one or multiple sources.
